design: Four arms warm-started from the SAME checkpoint (artifacts/checkpoints-v077-beta2-control/tt_tnt_step00010764.pkl), identical seed 5489, corpus tokens-v4, optimizer, --ddp 2, 1500 steps, 15 validation points each. Paired: same data order, so per-step oscillation cancels.
multiplicity: 6 pairwise contrasts reported, so the two-sided Bonferroni threshold is alpha=0.05/6, |t| > 2.64. Stated because two contrasts sit between 2.0 and 2.7 and would read as clearly significant uncorrected. B-learned vs D-frozen lands at 2.64 and is called BORDERLINE, not a pass.
confound: Every MoE arm introduces 204 fresh parameters and discards 18, so all three re-learn a feed-forward from init while the dense arm continues a converged one. The dense-vs-MoE gap is INITIALIZATION DEBT, not a quality verdict: it shrinks monotonically -0.523 -> -0.132 and is still shrinking at step 1500. Where the curves cross is NOT determined by this design. The MoE-vs-MoE contrasts are free of this confound because the debt is identical.
findings: Gate policy is a ~5% effect against the cost of replacing the FFN at all (0.012 nats vs 0.234).
Seeding the gate from die geography buys nothing measurable over random init: +0.0044 nats, |t|=2.0, signs 8+/7-, effect bounded under ~0.009 nats at 95%.

FREEZING the gate to die geography costs 0.0118 nats against a seeded-but-free gate (|t|=5.1, 14/15 signs) -- real, and ~15% of the run's own step-to-step floor of 0.077. A routing rule fixed by physical address is therefore nearly, but not quite, free.
